Fit covariance-aware K-means clusters on a frozen SOM

Source: R/SOMKMeans.R
CreateClusterModel_SOM_KMeans.Rd

Trains the established SOM, then fits K-means to equally weighted, whitened node profiles. The frozen regularized node covariance defines a shared Mahalanobis metric for node clustering. SOM training and best-matching-node assignment retain their original geometry.

Usage

CreateClusterModel_SOM_KMeans(
  data,
  variables = NULL,
  method = c("exploratory", "finalize"),
  k_range = 2:10,
  final_k = NULL,
  nstart = 50L,
  covariance_shrinkage = 0.05,
  ClusterVariableName = "Cluster",
  seed_som = 934521L,
  seed_kmeans = 93421L,
  stability_resamples = 0L,
  seed_stability = seed_som + 1L,
  stability_progress = FALSE,
  stability_cores = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing numeric clustering variables.

variables

Character vector of clustering variables.

method

Either "exploratory" or "finalize".

k_range

Candidate cluster counts in exploratory mode.

final_k

Explicit cluster count in finalize mode.

nstart

Number of K-means random starts; defaults to 50.

covariance_shrinkage

Number from zero to one, default 0.05. Covariance is shrunk toward a spherical matrix with the same average variance. Zero requires positive-definite node covariance.

ClusterVariableName

Name of the appended cluster column.

seed_som

Seed for SOM training.

seed_kmeans

Seed for node K-means fits; candidate k uses seed_kmeans + k.

stability_resamples

Number of full-pipeline 90% participant subsample refits.

seed_stability

Seed for participant subsampling.

stability_progress

Whether to print stability progress.

stability_cores

Worker count, or NULL for the shared memory-aware policy.

...

SOM preprocessing and map controls passed to CreateClusterModel_SOM_MClust(), including ZScoreType, som_xdim, som_ydim, som_epochs, and Relabel. Assignment is hard and node weighting is uniform; mixture and stability controls in ... are rejected.

Value

A Pipeline_SOM_KMeans object with ModelInfo, ModelInfo_KMeans, ModelInfo_SOM, fit_plot, Specification, and Stability. Finalized models include DataWithClusters and ProbFit. ModelInfo$Whitening freezes the node mean, raw and regularized covariance, and transforms. ModelInfo$fit_table reports whitened-node WSS, silhouette, Calinski-Harabasz, minimum node and participant counts, and size balance. ModelInfo$centers and profile figures use original SOM feature units; kmeans_model$centers uses whitened coordinates. cluster_sizes reports node and participant counts, including empty nodes.

Details

Participants inherit their frozen best-matching node's cluster. DistanceToCentroid measures participant distance to that cluster's centroid in the frozen Mahalanobis metric. AssignmentMargin is distance to the closest alternative centroid minus assigned-centroid distance; it can be negative. Flag_ProjectionDisagreement compares inherited assignment to nearest-centroid assignment without changing the label. Node* fields describe the corresponding node profile. These measures are not membership probabilities. SOM distance diagnostics remain in ModelInfo_SOM$SOMFit; centroid diagnostics are in ModelInfo$FitDiagnostics. Stability retrains scaling, the SOM, whitening, and K-means on participant subsamples with reference grid dimensions. It accompanies the initial recommendation without changing node labels after map assembly. External preprocessing supplied by the caller remains externally fixed during refits.

Stability output

Stability assesses internal reproducibility by full-pipeline 90% participant subsampling without replacement. For each replicate, 90% of complete participants are selected once, all preprocessing, any reduction (PCA, MCA, or SOM), and the selected clustering method are refit. Most pipelines compare assignments for sampled participants. SOM + Mclust instead maps the complete reference cohort onto every refit and compares the resulting full participant partition. Stability$settings$comparison_scope records the policy used. It is an internal sensitivity analysis, not independent-cohort validation.

Stability$settings records the analysis provenance:

  • resamples: requested number of 90% subsample refits.

  • seed: seed used to derive reproducible sampling and model seeds.

  • refit_scope: whether agreement is calculated directly in the refitted sample or after refit projection onto the reference cohort.

  • comparison_scope: the participants entering replicate agreement metrics; most pipelines use "sampled_participants", while SOM + Mclust uses "all_reference_participants".

  • resample_type: "subsample_without_replacement" for the primary stability analysis.

  • resample_fraction: the retained participant fraction, 0.90.

  • resample_fractions: every requested retention fraction. The default is 0.90; additional values create an opt-in deletion-stability curve without replacing the 90% primary screen.

  • coassignment_limit: maximum number of complete training participants (2,000) for which the full pairwise co-assignment matrix is calculated.

  • noise_policy: whether the method has noise labels. For ordinary methods it is "all clusters included"; HDBSCAN variants retain noise in ARI but exclude it from phenotype-level Jaccard recovery.

  • requested_cores, resolved_cores, and worker_policy: the requested and resolved refit workers and the reason for the resolution. Automatic resolution is capped by CPU, refit count, and the smaller of 50% physical RAM and 75% currently available RAM. Pairwise-memory methods are run serially automatically.

  • estimated_bytes_per_worker, estimated_total_bytes, physical_memory_bytes, available_memory_bytes, and safe_memory_budget_bytes: the conservative memory audit used to resolve automatic workers. An explicit worker request is preserved (within the CPU/scheduler cap) but warns if it exceeds the estimated safe budget.

Stability$replicates has one row per requested refit. Model and Classes identify the selected candidate (for HDBSCAN, Classes is the data-derived extracted count); Replicate is its sequence number; Status is "success" or a failure status; SamplingSeed and ModelSeed identify the participant draw and refit initialization policy; and Error contains the error message for an unsuccessful refit. ARI is the primary successful-refit metric: it is invariant to cluster numbering, higher is better, and it can be negative when agreement is worse than chance.

Stability$cluster_recovery has one row for each reference Cluster in each successful Replicate. Jaccard is the recovery of that reference cluster after matching it to the subsample cluster with the largest Jaccard overlap; higher is better and one is exact recovery. Model and Classes again identify the fitted candidate.

Stability$summary combines successful subsample refits: StabilitySuccessRate is successful refits divided by requested refits, an operational reliability measure that does not enter the reproducibility score. StabilityARI_Mean and StabilityARI_P05 are the mean and fifth percentile of ARI. StabilityJaccard_Mean and StabilityJaccard_Min are respectively the mean cluster-level recovery and the minimum of the cluster-specific mean recoveries across replicates. ReproducibilityScore does not include success rate. For most pipelines it is the mean of finite StabilityARI_Mean and StabilityJaccard_Mean values; SOM + Mclust uses StabilityARI_Mean directly because it selects on agreement of the final participant partition.

SOM + Mclust additionally returns StabilityARI_NonBoundary, StabilityARI_NonBoundary_P05, and non-boundary Jaccard summaries. These are secondary diagnostics calculated only on the fixed reference-model mask with SoftMargin below its threshold or SoftEntropy above its threshold excluded. The primary all-participant ARI always retains these boundary participants. boundary_summary reports their count and proportion overall and within each reference cluster. Earlier posterior-based Core fields are retained for compatibility as descriptive diagnostics; they are not the boundary-aware sensitivity measure.

Stability$failures repeats the replicate columns for unsuccessful refits, making fit failures auditable without mixing them with successful metrics.

Stability$participant_inclusion is one row per complete reference participant. .row_id identifies the merge-safe input row, Cluster its reference assignment, SuccessfulRefits the number of usable refits, and InclusionProbability the proportion of those refits in which the participant returned to that cluster's label-matched subsample cluster. Model and Classes identify the candidate. Higher inclusion is better.

Stability$cluster_inclusion summarizes inclusion within each reference Cluster: MeanInclusion, P05Inclusion, and MinInclusion are the mean, fifth percentile, and minimum participant inclusion probabilities; Model and Classes identify the candidate. Higher values indicate that all, not only the average, of a cluster is recovered consistently.

Stability$coassignment is available only when the complete training cohort has at most coassignment_limit participants. Each candidate entry has a status of "available", "skipped", or "not_available"; reason explains a non-available result; matrix is the pairwise probability that two complete reference participants are assigned together across successful subsample refits; and .row_id maps matrix rows and columns to the same identifiers returned in DataWithClusters and ProbFit$individual. Higher matrix values mean more consistent pairwise co-membership. Where more than one candidate is summarized, entries are named by its Model_Classes key. The matrix is diagnostic only and is never used for selection.

SOM + Mclust additionally returns memory-safe final-partition diagnostics for every cohort size. co_membership_by_cluster reports the proportion of within-reference-cluster participant pairs retained together (Cohesion) and the probability of co-assignment with outsiders (CrossMixing). co_membership_between_clusters reports cross-reference-cluster co-assignment probabilities. split_merge_reference and split_merge_refit identify dominant sources, shares, and effective numbers of groups, while profile_recovery reports matched-cluster correlation and RMSE for mean clustering-variable profiles on the frozen reference scale. These explain the nature of membership changes; they do not supersede ARI.

deletion_curve summarizes ARI, VI, NMI, and Fowlkes–Mallows agreement at each requested participant-retention fraction. It is useful for describing sensitivity to increasing cohort perturbation, not for selecting the least demanding fraction.

Stability$plots contains cluster_recovery (per-cluster Jaccard), partition_metrics (the ARI distribution), and cluster_inclusion; it also contains a co-assignment heatmap when the matrix is available. These diagnostics complement rather than replace ARI and Jaccard: none can turn a poorly reproducible cluster into a stable phenotype.

Metric sources: Hubert and Arabie (1985) define ARI; Jaccard (1901) defines the overlap coefficient; and Monti et al. (2003) describe resampling-based consensus co-assignment.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("SimulatedPhenotypeData")
model <- CreateClusterModel_SOM_KMeans(
  SimulatedPhenotypeData, paste0("Var", 1:6), method = "finalize",
  final_k = 4, som_xdim = 6, som_ydim = 6)
#> Warning: Explicit SOM dimensions (6 x 6 = 36 nodes) are below the floor of 10 nodes per clustering variable (60 nodes for 6 variables); diagnostics are retained for review.
projected <- ProjectCluster(model, SimulatedPhenotypeData)
#> far-from-map people, no group found; no far-from-map excess
projected$ProjectionFit$summary
